correctness.rationale: In each clique only the uniform vector and its normalized endpoint contrast enter; other contrasts have zero endpoint amplitude and are invariant. In the contrast/uniform basis this gives exactly K, B, D as displayed. With m=min(p,q), the two low energies of K have a gap bounded below in terms of fixed w>0, lie order m below D, and ||B||=O_w(m^-1/2). Weyl first isolates each low eigenvalue; eliminating the high component bounds its norm by O_w(m^-3/2) and gives a Schur correction O_w(m^-2), so the low eigenvalues and their low-sector normalized components differ from those of K by O_w(m^-2). Orthogonality gives low-sector weight O_w(m^-3/2) in each high eigenvector at the level of norm. This proves the low-low and mixed propagator bounds with no need for any separation between the two high eigenvalues. In the high-high block the first-order Duhamel correction vanishes and the double integral is bounded by t^2||B||^2/2; the cross-entry of exp(-itD) itself is at most |t|w/sqrt(pq). Endpoint overlap factors give O_{w,T}(m^-2) for both mixed and high-high amplitude contributions. Evaluating exp(-itK) gives the stated sign and phase; at pi/(2w) the sine differs from one by O_w(m^-2), giving the claimed probability. For fixed unequal p,q the conserved H^2 expectations p-1+w^2 and q-1+w^2 differ, precluding endpoint PGST. This proof is uniform for arbitrary ratios, not for variable w or growing time. evidence: Theorem 11 rules out single-bridge PST for nontrivial unweighted attachments; Theorem 13 deals with P_3. The corona theorem treats transfer between two fibre vertices of a looped complete base. The same-day sinc-window record has an all-to-all cross join and a time-averaged return observable. broader_coverage.reasoning: An absence-of-PST statement cannot imply absence of PGST, much less bounded-time amplitudes approaching one along changing dimensions. These finite-time or arithmetic transfer variants also have different graphs, propagators or quantifiers.

evidence: Earlier reductions use symmetric vertex orbits, but their dynamics include absorption or an oracle and generally fix equal sizes. The known one-bridge PST result is a fixed-graph obstruction. The unequal-clique exact absorber statement is infinite-time and Laplacian based.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new estimate is not a numerical readout from a covering size-asymptotic theorem in those sources. Even after recognizing the four orbit vectors, deriving it requires separating the low and high sectors with a size-uniform gap from min(p,q), controlling their cross-coupling, and suppressing the high-high transition after multiplication by the endpoint overlaps. The fixed unequal no-PGST corollary itself follows directly from a standard conserved moment and is not credited as an original theorem.

evidence: A weighted barbell or rooted K_2 construction is the same graph only when precisely one root-to-root edge joins two cliques. The closest indexed weighted bridge on the same unequal clique family, 97d03b674e6b, uses a Laplacian and a sink. The cited corona theorem instead has looped K_n as base with K_2 fibres.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The graph construction alone is not sufficient to identify the result: generators, target vertex states, observable and bounded time must be preserved. Standard PGST, perfect transfer, and fixed-time asymptotically high transfer as size grows are different quantifiers. The outbound lookup yielded no decisive source and is not negative evidence.

value.rationale: The phase-resolved estimate quantitatively distinguishes coherent single-edge transfer from time-optimized transfer on a fixed graph. It explains both the constant-time approach to unit probability and its leading size deficit, uniformly even for arbitrarily unbalanced cliques. A mere effective two-state heuristic would not give the second-order error or justify this leading loss; the conserved-moment contrast clarifies the noncommuting size and time questions.
